questions.text: Pointing to a photograph, Rekha said, "He is the only son of my grandfather's only daughter." How is the person in the photograph related to Rekha?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Decode backwards: "My grandfather's only daughter" = Mother; "Only son of Mother" = Brother (since 'He' is male). Full: Rekha's grandfather's only daughter is Rekha's mother. The only son of Rekha's mother is Rekha's brother. Hence the person is Rekha's brother.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select 'No improvement'. The RBI Governor emphasised on the need for immediate recapitalisation of public sector banks.
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Emphasise', 'Discuss', 'Order', 'Request', 'Approach' are transitive verbs — they take a direct object without any preposition. Step-by-step: 1) Recognise 'emphasise' as a transitive verb meaning 'to give special importance to'. 2) It directly governs the noun 'the need'. 3) Adding 'on', 'upon', or 'about' is grammatically redundant and incorrect in standard English. 4) Option A provides the correct direct object structure.

questions.text: Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. The curriculum aims at developing critical thinking, enhancing communication skills, and to foster leadership qualities among students.

options.label: A
options.text: The curriculum aims at developing critical thinking

questions.solution: Shortcut: Parallelism Check. Items in a list joined by 'and' must share the same grammatical form. The first two items are gerunds ('developing', 'enhancing') following 'aims at'. The third item must be a gerund ('fostering'), not an infinitive ('to foster'). Step-by-step: 1. Locate the list structure: 'aims at [1], [2], and [3]'. 2. Identify form of [1] and [2]: Gerunds (-ing). 3. Check [3]: 'to foster' (Infinitive). 4. Mismatch found. Correction: 'and fostering leadership qualities'. Error is in segment C.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. Neither the Branch Manager nor the clerks was available to address the customer's grievance regarding the failed transaction.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply the Proximity Rule for 'Neither...Nor' — the verb agrees with the nearest subject ('clerks', plural), so it must be 'were', not 'was'. Step-by-step: 1) Identify the correlative conjunction pair 'Neither...Nor'. 2) Locate the two subjects: 'Branch Manager' (singular) and 'clerks' (plural). 3) The verb follows the second subject ('clerks'). 4) 'Was' is singular; the plural verb 'were' is required. 5) Segment 'was available' contains the error.

questions.text: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is Rs. 120. What is the principal amount?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For 2 years, difference between CI and SI = P*(R/100)^2. Here 120 = P*(10/100)^2 => P = 120/0.01 = 12,000. Full: SI = P*10*2/100 = 0.2P. CI = P(1.1)^2 - P = 0.21P. Difference = 0.01P = 120 => P = 12,000.

questions.text: Statement: A ≥ B > C = D ≤ E < F Conclusions: I. A > D II. F > C

options.label: B
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Trace the inequality chain for each conclusion separately without drawing the full line. Full: For I: A ≥ B > C = D ⇒ A > D (True). For II: F > E ≥ D = C ⇒ F > C (True). Both conclusions follow.

questions.text: A train 200 metres long crosses a platform in 40 seconds. If the speed of the train is 54 km/h, what is the length of the platform?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Convert speed to m/s (54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s). Total distance = speed × time = 15 × 40 = 600 m. Platform length = total distance – train length = 600 – 200 = 400 m. Full steps: Speed = 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. In 40 seconds the train covers 15 × 40 = 600 m. This distance equals the length of the train plus the length of the platform. Hence platform length = 600 – 200 = 400 m.
questions.topic: Time, Speed and Distance - Train crossing platform

questions.text: Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F, and G sit in a straight row facing North. B sits third to the right of A, who sits at an extreme end. Only two persons sit between B and C. D sits immediately left of E. G sits to the right of F (not necessarily immediate). Who sits at the extreme right end of the row?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Fix A at left end (Pos 1) → B at Pos 4. Two persons between B(4) and C forces C at Pos 7 (Right end). Other conditions only fill middle seats. Full: A at extreme end (assume left, Pos 1). B is 3rd right → Pos 4. Two persons between B(4) and C → C at Pos 1 or 7. Pos 1 taken by A, so C at Pos 7 (Extreme Right). D/E and F/G occupy Pos 2,3,5,6 in valid orders, but C remains fixed at Right end.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of (7^95 × 3^58)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Unit digit of powers follows cycles of 4. 7^95 → 95 mod 4 = 3 → unit digit = 3 (7^3=343). 3^58 → 58 mod 4 = 2 → unit digit = 9 (3^2=9). Product unit digit = 3×9 = 27 → 7. Full steps: Cyclicity of 7 is 7,9,3,1; 95÷4 remainder 3 gives 3. Cyclicity of 3 is 3,9,7,1; 58÷4 remainder 2 gives 9. Multiplying the unit digits 3 and 9 gives 27, so final unit digit is 7.

questions.text: The investigation team decided to ______ the matter thoroughly before submitting the final report to the director.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use context elimination. The sentence demands a meaning of 'investigate/examine'. 'Look after' means care for, 'look up' means search/improve, 'look out' means be careful. Only 'look into' fits the investigation context. Step-by-step: 1. Identify the context: formal investigation. 2. Test each phrasal verb in the blank. 3. 'Look into the matter' = investigate the matter (Correct). 4. 'Look after the matter' = take care (Incorrect nuance). 5. 'Look up the matter' = search reference (Incorrect collocation). 6. 'Look out the matter' = meaningless here. Hence, Option A.

questions.text: Study the following arrangement carefully: K 4 # L M 3 @ N 2 $ O P 5 % Q R 6 ^ S T 7 & U How many such symbols are there each of which is immediately preceded by a number and immediately followed by a consonant?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan for pattern "Number → Symbol → Consonant". Vowels are A,E,I,O,U; rest letters are consonants. Full: Check each symbol: # (pre 4, next L→Cons) Yes; @ (pre 3, next N→Cons) Yes; $ (pre 2, next O→Vowel) No; % (pre 5, next Q→Cons) Yes; ^ (pre 6, next S→Cons) Yes; & (pre 7, next U→Vowel) No. Total = 4.

questions.text: Statements: Some Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. Some Pens are not Sharpeners. II. All Pencils can never be Sharpeners.

options.label: B
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply chain rules: Some + All = Some; Some + No = Some Not; All + No = No. Full: Some Pens are Pencils + All Pencils are Erasers ⇒ Some Pens are Erasers. This + No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ Some Pens are not Sharpeners (I follows). All Pencils are Erasers + No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ No Pencil is Sharpener ⇒ All Pencils can never be Sharpeners (II follows).

questions.text: After allowing two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on the marked price, an article is sold for Rs. 1296. What is the marked price of the article?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are equivalent to a single discount of 28% (1 – 0.8×0.9 = 0.28). Hence selling price = 72% of marked price → Marked price = 1296 / 0.72 = 1800. Full steps: Let marked price be x. After 20% discount price = 0.8x. After further 10% discount price = 0.9 × 0.8x = 0.72x. Given 0.72x = 1296, so x = 1296/0.72 = 1800.

questions.text: In the following questions, a word is given followed by four sentences. Choose the sentence in which the usage of the word is INCORRECT. PRECLUDE

options.label: A
options.text: The heavy rain will preclude the possibility of playing the match today.

options.label: B
options.text: His lack of experience does not preclude him from applying for the post.

options.label: C
options.text: The new evidence seems to preclude the theory proposed by the defence lawyer.

options.label: D
options.text: The contract precludes the tenant to sublet the apartment without permission.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Verb Pattern Elimination. 'Preclude' follows the fixed structure: 'Preclude [noun/pronoun] FROM [Verb-ing]'. Scan options for 'from + -ing'. Options A, B, C follow this pattern (A: possibility of playing ~ from playing; B: preclude him from applying; C: preclude the theory ~ implied from being accepted). Option D uses infinitive 'to sublet', violating the rule. Step-by-step: 1. Recall rule: Preclude + Object + From + Gerund. 2. Check A: 'preclude the possibility' (acceptable abstract usage). 3. Check B: 'preclude him from applying' (Perfect structure). 4. Check C: 'preclude the theory' (Acceptable). 5. Check D: 'precludes the tenant to sublet' (Incorrect, should be 'from subletting'). Option D is the answer.

questions.text: A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. B and C together can complete it in 15 days. C and A together can complete it in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Add the three pairwise efficiencies: (1/12+1/15+1/20) = (5+4+3)/60 = 12/60 = 1/5 per day for 2(A+B+C). So A+B+C = 1/10 per day. A's efficiency = (A+B+C) - (B+C) = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30 per day. Hence A alone takes 30 days. Full: Let total work = 60 units. A+B=5, B+C=4, C+A=3 units/day. Sum=12 => A+B+C=6. A=6-4=2 units/day. Time=60/2=30 days.
